properties.name: served_by.stale answers on macOS: currency is read from two signals, the /proc link and a startup fingerprint, and is unknown only when neither can be read
properties.rationale: ROOT CAUSE, from the record (fact:defect-currency-is-read-from-proc-self-exe-so-every-non-linux-run-answers-unknown-on-every-call): a Linux-only primitive used where the portable one already sat one module away, on a project whose accepted req:platform names macOS. Three candidates were tested; the old-build one was refuted, and both the mechanism (no fallback) and the amplifier (the note carried on every call) were confirmed. This fix reaches the CAUSE: on macOS the question now has an answer, so the per-call note disappears by construction rather than by suppression. WHAT IT TRADES: the fingerprint path reads a binary replaced by one of identical size and mtime as current — rare, and the Linux link path does not share it; the note says which path answered so a reader can weigh it. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: whether an UNKNOWN (both paths failing) should still be carried on every loop_status or once per session is a smaller separate question, untouched. NOT RUN ON macOS: the darwin behaviour is asserted through the pure function on a Linux box; Alex's next run is the real verification.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: exe_replaced_since_start (service.rs) read /proc/self/exe and nothing else, so on any non-Linux platform loop_status answered 'unknown, verify another way' on every call (Alex, macOS, v0.47.0). It now feeds a pure `currency_verdict(proc_link, start_fp, now_fp)`: STALE if the link carries ` (deleted)` OR the executable's size:mtime fingerprint differs from the one captured at process start; CURRENT only if the link is clean-or-absent AND fingerprints match-or-unavailable; UNKNOWN only when neither signal could be read. shared.rs gains `startup_fingerprint()` (a OnceLock initialised by `exe_fingerprint`, the portable primitive client election already used), called first thing in main so the value is genuinely the START one. Two new notes say WHICH check answered (FINGERPRINT_CURRENT_NOTE / FINGERPRINT_STALE_NOTE); UNKNOWN_NOTE now says both paths failed. The fingerprint also catches an in-place overwrite (same inode, clean link, moved mtime) that the link alone missed. STARTUP_FINGERPRINT is allowlisted in no_per_design_process_globals.rs with its reason (the executable is a fact about the process, not a design). Five pins in the_server_says_when_it_is_stale.rs, OBSERVED FAILING FIRST (E0425 — the function did not exist), then each branch pinned: no-proc+match -> current; no-proc+moved -> stale; neither -> unknown; deleted link wins; clean link + moved fingerprint -> stale. mcp 352/0, fmt/clippy clean.
